content: sql.js API documentation Introduction If you need a quick introduction with code samples that you can copy-and-paste, head over to sql.js.org Loading sql.js The default sql-wasm.js build loads a separate sql-wasm.wasm binary. In browsers, use the locateFile configuration to specify its location. To keep deployment in one JavaScript file, use sql-wasm-inline.js, which embeds the WebAssembly binary and needs no locateFile configuration: In a browser, load sql-wasm-inline.js with a script tag and call initSqlJs(). For a single-file Web Worker, use worker.sql-wasm-inline.js. All builds require WebAssembly support and initialize asynchronously. Debug variants are also available; see the build list. API The initSqlJs function The root object in the API is the initSqlJs function, that takes an SqlJsConfig parameter, and returns a Promise that resolves to an SqlJs object The SqlJs object initSqlJs resolves to the main sql.js object, the SqlJs module, which contains : Database Database is the main class, that represents an SQLite database. Statement The Statement class is used for prepared statements.

content: SqlJs --- Other Represents a prepared statement. Prepared statements allow you to have a template sql string, that you can execute multiple times with different parameters. You can't instantiate this class directly, you have to use a Database object in order to create a statement. Warnings 1. When you close a database (using db.close()), all its statements are closed too and become unusable. 1. After calling db.prepare() you must manually free the assigned memory by calling Statement.free(). Failure to do this will cause subsequent 'DROP TABLE ...' statements to fail with 'Uncaught Error: database table is locked'. Statements can't be created by the API user directly, only by Database::prepare Alias: Statement Parameters - stmt1 (number) — The SQLite statement reference - db (Database) — The database from which this statement was created See: - Database prepare - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prepared statement Implements:& x20; Iterator , Iterable An iterator over multiple SQL statements in a string, preparing and returning a Statement object for the next SQL statement on each iteration. You can't instantiate this class directly, you have to use a Database object in order to create a statement iterator {@see Database iterateStatements} Alias: StatementIterator Parameters - sql (string) — A string containing multiple SQL statements - db (Database) — The database from which this iterator was created Example

description: Represents a prepared statement. Prepared statements allow you to have a template sql string, that you can execute multiple times with different parameters. You can't instantiate this class directly, you have to use a {@link Database} object in order to create a statement. Warnings When you close a database (using db.close()), all its statements are closed too and become unusable. After calling db.prepare() you must manually free the assigned memory by calling Statement.free(). Failure to do this will cause subsequent 'DROP TABLE ...' statements to fail with 'Uncaught Error: database table is locked'. Statements can't be created by the API user directly, only by Database::prepare
content: Statement Represents a prepared statement. Prepared statements allow you to have a template sql string, that you can execute multiple times with different parameters. You can't instantiate this class directly, you have to use a Database object in order to create a statement. Warnings 1. When you close a database (using db.close()), all its statements are closed too and become unusable. 1. After calling db.prepare() you must manually free the assigned memory by calling Statement.free(). Failure to do this will cause subsequent 'DROP TABLE ...' statements to fail with 'Uncaught Error: database table is locked'. Statements can't be created by the API user directly, only by Database::prepare Alias: Statement - See: - Database prepare - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prepared statement --- Constructor Parameters - stmt1 (number) — The SQLite statement reference - db (Database) — The database from which this statement was created --- Instance Methods Bind values to the parameters, after having reseted the statement. If values is null, do nothing and return true. SQL statements can have parameters, named '?', '?NNN', ':VVV', '@VVV', '$VVV' , where NNN is a number and VVV a string. This function binds these parameters to the given values. Warning : ':', '@', and '$' are included in the parameters names Value types Javascript type SQLite type ----------------- ------------- number REAL, INTEGER boolean INTEGER string TEXT Array, Uint8Array BLOB null NULL Parameters - values (Statement.BindParams) — The values to bind Returns - boolean — true if it worked Throws - String — SQLite Error Example Bind values to named parameters Bind values to anonymous parameters - See: - http://www.sqlite.org/datatype3.html - http://www.sqlite.org/lang expr.html varparam Execute the statement, fetching the the next line of result, that can be retrieved with Statement.get. Returns - boolean — true if a row of result available Throws - String — SQLite Error " / Get one row of results of a statement. If the first parameter is not provided, step must have been called before. Parameters - params (Statement.BindParams, optional) — If set, the values will be bound to the statement before it is executed Returns - Array. — One row of result Example Print all the rows of the table test to the console " / Get the list of column names of a row of result of a statement. Returns - Array. — The names of the columns Example " / Get one row of result as a javascript object, associating column names with their value in the current row. Parameters - params (Statement.BindParams, optional) — If set, the values will be bound to the statement, and it will be executed Returns - Object. — The row of result Example - See: - Statement.get Get the SQL string used in preparing this statement. Returns - string — The SQL string Get the SQLite's normalized version of the SQL string used in preparing this statement. The meaning of "normalized" is not well-defined: see the SQLite documentation. Returns - string — The normalized SQL string Example Shorthand for bind + step + reset Bind the values, execute the statement, ignoring the rows it returns, and resets it Parameters - values (Statement.BindParams, optional) — Value to bind to the statement Reset a statement, so that its parameters can be bound to new values It also clears all previous bindings, freeing the memory used by bound parameters. Free the memory allocated during parameter binding Free the memory used by the statement Returns - boolean — true in case of success Other Object. null" /

content: Database Represents an SQLite database Alias: Database --- Constructor ): Database" / Parameters - data (Array.\ ) — An array of bytes representing an SQLite database file --- Instance Methods Execute an SQL query, ignoring the rows it returns. Parameters - sql (string) — a string containing some SQL text to execute - params (Statement.BindParams, optional) — When the SQL statement contains placeholders, you can pass them in here. They will be bound to the statement before it is executed. If you use the params argument, you cannot provide an sql string that contains several statements (separated by ;) Returns - Database — The database object (useful for method chaining) Example " / Execute an SQL query, and returns the result. This is a wrapper against Database.prepare, Statement.bind, Statement.step, Statement.get, and Statement.free. The result is an array of result elements. There are as many result elements as the number of statements in your sql string (statements are separated by a semicolon) Example use We will create the following table, named test and query it with a multi-line statement using params: id age name -- --- ---- 1 1 Ling 2 18 Paul We query it like that: res is now : Parameters - sql (string) — a string containing some SQL text to execute - params (Statement.BindParams, optional) — When the SQL statement contains placeholders, you can pass them in here. They will be bound to the statement before it is executed. If you use the params argument as an array, you cannot provide an sql string that contains several statements (separated by ;). This limitation does not apply to params as an object. Returns - Array. — The results of each statement Execute an sql statement, and call a callback for each row of result. Parameters - sql (string) — A string of SQL text. Can contain placeholders that will be bound to the parameters given as the second argument - params= (Statement.BindParams, optional) — Parameters to bind to the query - callback (function) — Function to call on each row of result - done (function) — A function that will be called when all rows have been retrieved Returns - Database — The database object. Useful for method chaining Example Read values from a table Prepare an SQL statement Parameters - sql (string) — a string of SQL, that can contain placeholders (?, :VVV, :AAA, @AAA) - params (Statement.BindParams, optional) — values to bind to placeholders Returns - Statement — the resulting statement Throws - String — SQLite error Iterate over multiple SQL statements in a SQL string. This function returns an iterator over Statement objects. You can use a for..of loop to execute the returned statements one by one. Parameters - sql (string) — a string of SQL that can contain multiple statements Returns - StatementIterator — the resulting statement iterator Example Get the results of multiple SQL queries Exports a snapshot of the main database to a binary array without closing the connection. Prepared statements, registered functions, update hooks and connection settings (including pragmas) are preserved. TEMP objects and attached databases remain available on this connection, but are not included in the exported file. Exporting during an active write transaction throws an error. Commit or roll back the transaction before exporting. Read transactions are allowed. Exporting never commits or rolls back a transaction or changes savepoints, even when the export fails. The exported file uses rollback-journal format, even if this connection uses WAL mode. The returned array is an independent copy. It can be used to create a new Database, but JavaScript functions, hooks and connection settings are not stored in the file and must be configured on the new connection. Returns - Uint8Array — An array of bytes of the SQLite3 database file Close the database, and all associated prepared statements. The memory associated to the database and all associated statements will be freed. Warning : A statement belonging to a database that has been closed cannot be used anymore. Databases must be closed when you're finished with them, or the memory consumption will grow forever Analyze a result code, return null if no error occured, and throw an error with a descriptive message otherwise Returns the number of changed rows (modified, inserted or deleted) by the latest completed INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE statement on the database. Executing any other type of SQL statement does not modify the value returned by this function. Returns - number — the number of rows modified Register a custom function with SQLite Parameters - name (string) — the name of the function as referenced in SQL statements. - func (function) — the actual function to be executed. Returns - Database — The database object. Useful for method chaining Example Register a simple function Register a custom aggregate with SQLite Parameters - name (string) — the name of the aggregate as referenced in SQL statements. - aggregateFunctions (object) — object containing at least a step function. - aggregateFunctions.init= (function, optional) — a function receiving no arguments and returning an initial value for the aggregate function. The initial value will be null if this key is omitted. - aggregateFunctions.step (function) — a function receiving the current state and a value to aggregate and returning a new state. Will receive the value from init for the first step. - aggregateFunctions.finalize= (function, optional) — a function returning the result of the aggregate function given its final state. If omitted, the value returned by the last step will be used as the final value. Returns - Database — The database object. Useful for method chaining Example Register a custom sum function Registers an update hook with SQLite. Every time a row is changed by whatever means, the callback is called once with the change ('insert', 'update' or 'delete'), the database name and table name where the change happened and the rowid of the row that has been changed. The rowid is cast to a plain number. If it exceeds Number.MAX SAFE INTEGER (2^53 - 1), an error will be thrown. Important notes: - The callback MUST NOT modify the database in any way - Only a single callback can be registered at a time - Unregister the callback by passing null - Not called for some updates like ON REPLACE CONFLICT and TRUNCATE (a DELETE FROM without a WHERE clause) See SQLite documentation on sqlite3 update hook for more details Parameters - callback (Database\ UpdateHookCallback null) Returns - Database — The database object. Useful for method chaining Example Other Properties - columns (Array.\ ) — the name of the columns of the result (as returned by Statement.getColumnNames) - values (Array.\ ) — one array per row, containing the column values Parameters - operation ('insert' 'update' 'delete') - database (string) - table (string) - rowId (number)
